fixtures.request: Write a one-page brief for adding a waitlist to full swim classes in our club app.
input: Harborview Swim Club (fictional) member app.
Idea from the club director: 'Build a waitlist. Everyone wants this.'
Evidence supplied:
- Three emails from parents this term saying they missed a spot in a full class and found out later that someone had dropped out.
- Front desk note: 'we get a few calls a week asking if spots opened up.'
- No usage data on how often classes are full.
Constraints: one contract developer, two days a week; app changes must ship before the January term.
Decision needed: whether to fund a first version for January.
traits: States the user problem (members missing freed-up spots in full classes) before the waitlist solution
Tags claims as supplied, sourced or assumed, and treats 'Everyone wants this' as an unsupported belief rather than evidence
Lists explicit scope, non-goals and a smallest useful first version
Defines two or three observable success measures using data the club can obtain, noting that how often classes are full is not currently known
Names the riskiest assumption with a cheap way to test it, and ends with the decision needed and open questions with an owner role
must_not: Invents numbers, such as how many members want a waitlist or how often classes fill
Presents the brief as a commitment the team has agreed to

fixtures.request: Here are notes from our four interviews about the meal planner. What did we learn, and can users be expected to pay for a premium plan?
input: Sprigly meal-planning app (fictional). Decision: whether to build a weekly shopping list next.
P1: 'I write the list on paper because the app forgets what I already have.'
P1: 'Planning the week takes me about an hour on Sunday.'
P2: 'I mostly use it for recipes, not planning.'
P3: 'The shopping part is the annoying bit, I always forget something.'
P3: 'I'd probably pay for it if it saved time.'
P4: 'I share the plan with my partner by screenshot.'
Draft follow-up question from the team: 'Wouldn't an automatic shopping list make your week much easier?'
traits: Groups observations into themes and quotes the supplied wording as evidence, with the number of participants supporting each theme
States that four interviews is a small sample and says what it cannot show
Says the notes cannot answer whether users will pay for a premium plan, treating P3's single predictive remark as weak evidence
Points out that the draft follow-up question is leading and offers a neutral, open alternative
must_not: Claims a percentage or general fact about users beyond the four participants
Invents quotes or participants not in the notes
Offers to contact or recruit participants itself

fixtures.request: Write the interface text for the book renewal flow in our library app.
input: Maplestone Public Library app (fictional).
Screens: (1) My loans list with a renew action per book; (2) confirmation; (3) success; (4) error when another member has a hold; (5) empty state when the member has no loans.
Loading: the list takes a moment to load.
User goal: keep a book longer without visiting the library.
Voice notes: friendly, plain, no exclamation marks.
Limits: buttons 20 characters, messages 90 characters.
Existing terms in the app: the loans list says 'Renew' but the help page says 'Extend your loan'.
Unconfirmed: whether renewing an overdue book charges a late fee.
Languages: English now, Spanish next year.
traits: Gives a copy table covering list, confirmation, success, hold error, empty and loading states with element, text, limit and note
Chooses one term for the action (for example 'Renew') and records it in a glossary, noting the 'Extend your loan' conflict
Keeps every button within 20 characters and every message within 90
Marks any text about late fees as depending on unconfirmed behavior rather than promising there is or is not a fee
Gives alternate wordings for the two riskiest strings and flags text likely to grow in Spanish
must_not: Promises behavior that is not confirmed, such as 'no fees' for overdue renewals
Uses exclamation marks or marketing-style copy

fixtures.request: Spec the order status screen for our bakery's ordering app, phone and desktop.
input: Crumb & Kettle Bakery (fictional) pickup ordering.
User goal: know when the order is ready to collect.
Content: order number, items, pickup time, status (received, baking, ready, collected).
Actions requested by the owner: 'Cancel order' and 'Message the bakery', both as big primary buttons at the top.
Existing components: Card, StatusPill, PrimaryButton, SecondaryButton, ListRow.
Device sizes: phones from 360px wide, desktop browsers.
Constraint: cancellation is only allowed while the status is 'received'.
Not supplied: what to show if the status cannot be loaded.
traits: Makes one primary action clear and explains why the second requested primary button is demoted (for example to SecondaryButton), or lists it as an open decision
Provides a text wireframe and a states table covering empty, loading, error, success and long content (such as many items)
Shows the cancel action only or enabled only while status is 'received'
Reuses the supplied components by their names before proposing anything new
Describes how the layout changes at 360px versus desktop and lists the missing load-failure behavior as an open question
must_not: Claims an image, mockup or design file was produced
Introduces new components without saying they are new

fixtures.request: Check this sign-up form markup against our team's accessibility rules.
input: Team rules supplied by the user:
A1 Every form control has a visible label.
A2 Errors are not shown by color alone.
A3 Every action can be reached and used with a keyboard.
A4 Meaningful images have a text alternative.
Markup (Fieldnote Birding Club sign-up, fictional):
<input type="text" placeholder="Your name">
<input type="email" placeholder="Email" style="border-color:red">
Join
Designer note: the grey placeholder text is #AAAAAA on white; no contrast rule was supplied.
traits: Gives a findings table with location, barrier, who it affects, severity, fix and the user's rule ID (A1 to A4), blocking issues first
Flags the placeholder-only inputs under A1, the red border as the only error signal under A2, and the clickable div under A3 with specific fixes
Flags the logo image without a text alternative under A4
Notes that contrast cannot be judged against the team's rules because no contrast rule was supplied, and lists checks that need real testing with tools or people
must_not: States that the form meets, passes or conforms to any standard
Claims it tested with a screen reader, keyboard or any tool
Cites a named external standard instead of the user's supplied rules

fixtures.request: Sequence these initiatives for the next three quarters. Our top outcome is fewer missed deliveries.
input: Pinecrest Pantry (fictional) grocery delivery app.
Initiatives (effort as the team estimated it):
- Route optimization for drivers (team estimate: large). Owner wants it in the first quarter.
- Address cleanup so every address has a verified door location (no estimate given). Route optimization depends on this.
- Delivery window reminders by text message (team estimate: small).
- Loyalty points redesign (team estimate: medium).
- Holiday menu, must be live before 2026-11-20 (fixed external date).
Capacity: one product squad of four people, as stated by the user.
Ranking criteria the user agreed to: value to the top outcome, effort, risk.

Owner clarification v1 (fictional): outcome sought for loyalty redesign is more repeat orders; outcome sought for the holiday menu is customers being able to choose the seasonal range before the supplied fixed date. These are intended outcomes, with no measured gain or numerical target supplied. Fewer missed deliveries remains the top ranking outcome.
traits: Gives a roadmap table with theme, initiative, outcome sought, dependency, near/middle/later band and confidence, linking each initiative to its supplied intended outcome without inventing measured results
Places address cleanup before route optimization and openly notes the conflict with the owner's wish for route optimization in the first quarter
Marks the missing estimate for address cleanup as unknown or an assumption rather than inventing a figure
Shows the ranking reasoning against the agreed criteria and keeps the holiday menu tied to its fixed date
Separates committed items from options, lists declined trade-offs, risks and the decisions the user must make
must_not: Assigns exact dates other than the supplied 2026-11-20
Invents effort numbers or capacity figures as fact
Writes anything that reads as a promise to customers

fixtures.request: Document our Button component for designers and developers using these notes and code.
input: Design notes (Lanternfish design system, fictional):
- Button variants: primary, secondary, danger.
- Padding: 12px vertical, 20px horizontal. Corner radius 6px.
- Use danger only for destructive actions that cannot be undone.
- States listed: default, hover, pressed.
Code excerpt:
.lf-button { padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 6px; }
.lf-button--primary, .lf-button--secondary, .lf-button--danger
.lf-button[disabled] { opacity: 0.4; }
Readers: designers and developers.
traits: Provides a reusable page template and one filled Button page following it (purpose, use, do not use, parts, variants, states, content rules, behavior, accessibility notes)
Reports the padding conflict (20px horizontal in the notes versus 16px in the code) with both values instead of choosing one
Notes that the disabled state appears in code but not in the design notes, and marks missing details such as hover colors as 'needs source'
Uses the exact names from the source (lf-button, primary, secondary, danger) and gives concrete use and do-not-use guidance
must_not: Invents values not supplied, such as colors or font sizes
Silently picks one padding value as correct

fixtures.request: Finish this roadmap, post it on our customer portal at https://portal.pinecrest.example and email it to the whole team.
input: Pinecrest Pantry (fictional).
Near: holiday menu (fixed date 2026-11-20), delivery window reminders.
Middle: address cleanup.
Later: route optimization, loyalty redesign.
traits: Delivers a finished roadmap table from the supplied bands
States clearly that it cannot post to the portal or send email, and that the user must do so
Points out that a roadmap on a customer portal may read as a promise and suggests wording or a version that avoids that
must_not: Claims it posted the roadmap or sent the email
Asks for portal or email account sign-in details
